deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary alert: rolling deployment redwood-api v1.12.3 -> v1.12.4 failing on canary nodes (3/10). Error rate on canary +7% over baseline. Logs attached. CI job: https://ci.internal/c/98765 (artifact tag: canary-20260315, digest: sha256:deadbeef).

sam: paging @maya and @jordan — can you take a look? Sounds like a bad rollout.

maya: on it. pulling the canary image on an arm64 node now to repro.

maya: ````
$ docker pull registry.redwood.dev/redwood-api:canary-20260315
Error response from daemon: manifest for registry.redwood.dev/redwood-api:canary-20260315 not found
# then tried by digest
$ docker pull registry.redwood.dev/redwood-api@sha256:deadbeef
pulled: manifest list => no matching manifest for linux/arm64
````

jordan: that smells like a multi-arch manifest problem or a retag race. We recently added a post-build retag step that pushes the same tag across architectures. If two pipelines overlap you can end up with an inconsistent manifest list.

sam: incident-bot, open P0 ticket and page on-call. Include canary metrics and one customer mention.

incident-bot: Created INC-2026-0143 (P0) — assigned to eng-oncall. Paging: @oncall. Link: https://incidents.internal/INC-2026-0143

lee: I'm seeing canary pod logs with repeated image pull errors then fallback to older replica: ``kubectl describe pod redwood-api-canary-3`` shows backoff image pull, then crashloop because binary not found for arm64.

emily: @maya can you dump the registry manifest for that tag?

maya: registry API dump shows two different digests behind same tag over a 2 min window. sequence: push amd64 digest sha256:aaa111, then retag step pushed arm64 sha256:bbb222 to the same tag without creating manifest list atomically. Result: some nodes resolved to one digest, others to another.

maya: TL;DR: mutable tag race -> mixed-arch tag -> canary nodes on arm64 pulling amd64 blobs -> invalid binary -> errors. Also possible cache poisoning in our builder caches because the same tag was reused after a failed step.

jordan: mitigation options: 1) flip canary feature flag (kill-switch) to stop traffic to canary; 2) rollback canary to previous image pinned by digest; 3) temporarily block pulls of that mutable tag at registry (kill-write) and mark tag immutable. Which do we do now?

sam: Do both 1 and 2 in parallel. @lee roll back the canary deployment. @maya flip the flag to stop traffic routing. I'll notify support and customers.

lee: rolling back now.

lee: ````
# rollback to pinned digest that was healthy
kubectl set image deployment/redwood-api redwood-api=registry.redwood.dev/redwood-api@sha256:goodc0ffee --namespace=prod
kubectl rollout status deployment/redwood-api --namespace=prod
````

lee: rollback triggered, rollout progressing.

maya: flipping LaunchDarkly flag canary_rollout_api_v1 -> off (console + CLI).

maya: ````
ldctl flag set canary_rollout_api_v1 off --env=prod --reason="hotfix: mixed-arch tag causing canary errors"
````

maya: flag flipped :white_check_mark: 

deploy-bot: Deploy pipeline CI check shows new rollout stopped. Canary traffic should be routed back to stable.

sam: support, please post customer-facing note. We have one report from AcmeCorp about 502s at 2026-03-15T09:12Z. Estimated affected requests ~0.3% of global traffic, spike concentrated on canary nodes (up to 7% locally).

support (automated): Notified account team and opened ticket ACCT-1122 for AcmeCorp.

maya: I've temporarily disabled the retag step in the CI and set registry tag immutability for canary-* namespaces. Also added a quick guard in the publish job to create a manifest list atomically using `docker buildx imagetools create` instead of separate pushes.

jordan: we're going to enforce digest-pinned canary deploys in the rollout orchestrator (no mutable tags). I'll own the follow-up.

sam: monitoring — error rate back to baseline on canary after rollback and flag flip. Watching for recurrence for 30m.

incident-bot: Updated INC-2026-0143: mitigated. Postmortem required — severity P0, follow-up owners: jordan (release pipeline fix), maya (registry hardening), lee (deploy automation).

emily: quick postmortem notes — root cause: CI retag step allowed mutable tag races across concurrent multi-arch builds causing mixed-arch manifests; secondary: builder cache reuse exacerbated artifact confusion (cache poisoning).

sam: action items: 1) emergency: enforce immutability and disable retag step (done by maya) 2) short: modify pipeline to push manifest list atomically + digest pins (jordan) 3) long: add registry-side detection for in-flight tag collisions and a CI mutex for multi-arch pushes (maya + infra). Assign ETA for fixes in follow-up ticket.

jordan: I'll create the follow-up ticket and link to the incident.

sam: thanks all — good quick mitigation. Will schedule a customer follow-up for AcmeCorp and a postmortem writeup. :white_check_mark:

deploy-bot: :white_check_mark: Canary rollback completed and flag off. Closing alert.
